WRITE.definition_en: Proper names of individuals whose primary role is in literature, such as novelists, scriptwriters, poets. If the person is a literary professional, use WRITE instead of PER.

BOOK.definition_en: Titles of literary works published as books, including novels and book-length collections.

POEM.definition_en: Titles of poetic works, including individual poems or recognized poetry collections.

GENRE.definition_en: Named literary genres and subgenres serving as categories.

MAG.definition_en: Proper names of magazines or periodicals that publish literary works.

AWARD.definition_en: Proper names of awards in the field of literature.

EVENT.definition_en: Named events related to literature such as festivals, readings, or conferences.

PER.definition_en: Proper names of individuals not categorized as WRITE.

ORG.definition_en: Official names of organizations, institutions, or groups not falling into MAG.

MISC.definition_en: Residual named entities in the literature domain that do not fit AWARD, BOOK, CTRY, EVENT, GENRE, LOC, MAG, ORG, PER, POEM, or WRITE. Use sparingly and only for clearly named entities that lack a more specific label.

final_task_goal: The objective of this NER scheme is to annotate literature-related Wikipedia texts to support downstream linking and database construction. The labels enable reliable entity linking and knowledge-graph building across writers, works, genres, magazines, awards, and events, as well as general entities (persons, organizations, locations, countries). These structured annotations will power bibliographic integration, author–work–genre graph construction, and enhanced retrieval in literature-focused knowledge bases.
